candidates.source_name: CRPS — Centralni registar privrednih subjekata (public entity search)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory company register of Montenegro; single authoritative record of legal form, status (aktivan / u stečaju / u likvidaciji / brisan), founding date, registered seat and legal representatives for every bank, payment institution, fintech and vendor subsidiary operating in ME. Baseline entity spine for the whole A1 workstream.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic keyed lookup by company name/PIB for a watchlist of ME banks, PSPs and IT vendors; parse the entity detail page. Rate-limit politely; no known bulk export.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from CRPS portal pages

candidates.why_relevant: Explains what must be filed, by whom, on which forms, and under which law; publishes registry notices (e.g. establishment of the beneficial-owner register on 1 Aug 2021). Best pointer for understanding coverage and completeness of ME statutory filings.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl of /strana/pregled/* and /preuzimanja/pregled for procedure and form changes.

candidates.source_name: eFirma — CRPS electronic company portal
candidates.why_relevant: The transactional front end of the register (e-registration, e-extracts, beneficial owners). Indicates digitisation level of ME registry and is the channel through which official extracts (izvod) can be ordered for named financial-sector entities.
candidates.access_status: partly_authenticated (digital certificate required for filing; some search public)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/assisted use for targeted extracts; monitor portal notices. Do not automate authenticated areas.

candidates.source_name: Registar stvarnih vlasnika (Register of Beneficial Owners), CRPS
candidates.why_relevant: UBO data for all ME legal entities, established 1 Aug 2021 under the AML/CFT law. The only structured way to see who really controls unlisted payment firms, exchange offices, agent networks and vendor subsidiaries.

candidates.suggested_collection_method: Targeted lookups per watchlist entity; snapshot UBO records annually and diff for control changes.

negative_findings.description: Direct fetch of the CRPS public search portal (http://www.pretraga.crps.me/) failed with an OpenSSL TLSV1_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR when the request was upgraded to HTTPS.
negative_findings.result_summary: Could not retrieve the page body; the field structure of the public search form and result pages remains undocumented in this slice. The domain appears repeatedly in current search results, so the hypothesis is a legacy/misconfigured TLS stack or bot defence, not a dead site.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated collector against CRPS will need a tolerant TLS client (or plain HTTP) and should not be designed assuming a modern HTTPS endpoint.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Montenegrin for a public, free search interface over FILED annual financial statements held by the tax authority (terms: 'pretraga finansijskih iskaza', 'javna objava finansijskih iskaza', 'pregled finansijskih iskaza').
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the filing-side portal (eprijava.tax.gov.me/TaxisPortal) and the desktop filing application were found; no evidence of a free public per-company statement lookup equivalent to Serbia's APR or Croatia's RGFI. Commercial redistributors (bilansi.me, boniteti.me, companywall.me) fill this gap, which is itself indirect evidence that no free public search exists.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Entity-level ME financial statements likely require paid vendors or FOI requests; a scraping-first collection design would fail.

negative_findings.description: Looked for an official CRPS API, bulk download or open-data dump of the company register.
negative_findings.result_summary: No official API or bulk endpoint surfaced. Machine-readable access appears to exist only via third parties (OpenCorporates register #168, CompanyData.com) rather than from the registry itself.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines build-vs-buy for the ME entity spine and adds licence cost/terms as a dependency.

negative_findings.description: Searched MONSTAT in Montenegrin for a dedicated structural-business-statistics or financial-institutions release page (terms: 'strukturne poslovne statistike', 'finansijsko posredovanje', 'finansijske institucije').
negative_findings.result_summary: MONSTAT's business-register methodology and general publication/yearbook pages were located, but no specific landing page for NACE-K financial-activity aggregates was confirmed. Most ME financial-sector aggregates appear to originate with the central bank rather than MONSTAT.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sector aggregates for banking/payments may have to be taken from CBCG (a different coverage cell) with MONSTAT used only for enterprise counts and business demography.

negative_findings.description: The Register of Beneficial Owners at efirma.tax.gov.me is described as searchable, but sources also say registration and extract-ordering require a registered digital certificate.
negative_findings.result_summary: Could not determine from public pages whether anonymous public search of UBO records is available or whether all lookups are certificate-gated.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ownership-chain analysis for unlisted ME payment firms may require a Montenegrin digital certificate or a local partner.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-attempt with a permissive TLS client and plain HTTP, and via a browser session; document the search form parameters and result-page schema.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed lawful, scalable channel for obtaining filed annual accounts of unlisted ME banks, payment institutions and vendor subsidiaries.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Trial bilansi.me and boniteti.me with a 10-entity watchlist; in parallel test a FOI request (zahtjev za slobodan pristup informacijama) to Uprava prihoda i carina for filed statements of named entities, to establish whether filings are public documents.

coverage_gaps.description: A new Zakon o računovodstvu (Sl. list CG 84/2025, in force 8 Aug 2025) postdates most of the filing-procedure material found, which is largely 2020-2021 vintage.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Read the 2025 law and any new Pravilnik to confirm current deadlines, forms, audit thresholds and — critically — whether it introduces public disclosure of financial statements.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the cell with searches for 'registar zaloga Crna Gora', 'Centralna depozitarna agencija akcionari banke', 'registar ovlašćenih revizora Ministarstvo finansija'.

brief: Montenegro's statutory filing landscape is centralised but only half-open: CRPS (pretraga.crps.me / eFirma) is the authoritative company and beneficial-owner register and is publicly searchable, while the annual financial statements themselves are filed to the Uprava prihoda i carina via the TaxisPortal/ePrijava system with no confirmed free public per-company lookup. The practical consequence is a two-track collection design — registry identity and ownership scraped or licensed from CRPS/OpenCorporates, and actual financials bought from local redistributors (bilansi.me, boniteti.me, companywall.me) or requested under freedom-of-information. MONSTAT supplies the aggregate layer via its statistical business register and yearbook, though NACE-K financial-sector aggregates appear to originate with the central bank rather than the statistics office. Two live risks: the CRPS portal failed TLS negotiation in this session (unverified, likely bot-defended rather than dead), and a new Zakon o računovodstvu in force since 8 August 2025 may have changed filing and disclosure rules relative to most documentation found.
